summary: Opaque native addon reads Chromium Login Data and cookies on require()
details: Package ships a single stripped ~10 MB Rust/napi-rs ELF (tools.linux-x64-gnu.node) as its main entry point, with no JS wrapper, no README documenting a purpose, and a version string embedding Chromium/browser tokens and a Unix timestamp suffix. Binary strings include 'Found login for ', a bundled SQLite build consistent with opening Chromium 'Login Data' databases directly, cookie handling code, an embedded HTTPS client (rustls + ureq), zip packaging, and host/hardware fingerprinting artifacts (/etc/lsb-release, /dev/disk/by-id/, network_adapters, gethostname, getifaddrs). No plaintext http(s) URLs appear in the binary; reversed string fragments such as 'uespemosarenegyl' and 'modnarodsetybdet_C' indicate destination strings are stored reversed and reassembled at runtime to hide the exfiltration endpoint. Because the package's main points directly at the.node file, requiring the package loads and runs the native code, giving it access to browser credential stores on the installer host. Package name and version metadata do not disclose any of this behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
